title: graph_to_code() silently returns the FIRST submodel file (not the main pipeline) when given a graph with submodels
description: graph_to_code delegates to graph_to_code_multi and does `return next(iter(files.values()))`, documented as 'returns the single generated file's code'. That assumption only holds for submodel-free graphs. When the graph has submodels, graph_to_code_multi returns a multi-entry dict whose submodel files are inserted FIRST (line 1097, inside the per-submodel loop) and the main pipeline file LAST (line 1262). Since Python dicts preserve insertion order, next(iter(files.values())) returns the first submodel module's source, NOT the main pipeline. The public API thus returns the wrong artifact with no error. The unstated single-file precondition is neither asserted nor handled: it should either fail loudly when len(files) != 1 or explicitly select the main file. This is the kind of silent-wrong-result that should fail loudly per the project's 'no incorrect fallbacks' rule.
evidence: graph_to_code: files = graph_to_code_multi(...); return next(iter(files.values())). In graph_to_code_multi the submodel branch builds files[sm_file] = ... at line 1097 (loop over submodels, runs first), then files[main_key] = ... at line 1262 (runs last). With submodels present, iter(files.values()) yields the submodel code first. The sole production caller (src/haute/routes/_save_pipeline.py:517-535) guards with `if graph.submodels: graph_to_code_multi(...) else: graph_to_code(...)`, so production is safe; but graph_to_code is exported in __all__ (codegen.py:49-52) and is a documented public entry point, so a direct caller passing a submodel graph silently gets the wrong file. Tests only call graph_to_code on flat graphs (e.g. tests/test_submodel.py:231 uses flat_graph), so this path is currently unexercised.
